rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoopoe's confident correction of Solomon despite its weakness shows knowledge's honor: even a lowly learner gains a forceful voice before rulers.
rows.anchor: فلولا أن العلم أشرف الأشياء وإلا فمن أين للهدهد أن يتكلم في مجلس سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's comparison of an hour's reflection with sixty years of worship favors reflection because it brings one to God, while worship brings one to God's reward; alternatively, heart-work outranks bodily action.
rows.anchor: تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة ستين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer serves inward remembrance, so its end is nobler than its means; this supports the superiority of knowledge and reflection.
rows.anchor: جعل الصلاة وسيلة إلى ذكر القلب والمقصود أشرف من الوسيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an calls knowledge great and wisdom abundant good; al-Razi identifies wisdom with knowledge.
rows.anchor: فسمى العلم عظيما وسمي الحكمة خيرا كثيرا فالحكمة هي العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering of Quranic teaching before the other blessings signals that knowledge is superior to them.
rows.anchor: فجعل هذه النعمة مقدمة على جميع النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says all revealed scriptures speak of knowledge's merit.
rows.anchor: أن سائر كتب الله ناطقة بفضل العلم

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A saying attributed to God in the Torah tells Moses to magnify wisdom, learn it, practice it, and share it to gain divine honor in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: عظم الحكمة فإني لا أجعل الحكمة في قلب عبد إلا وأردت أن أغفر له

rows.speaker: الله سبحانه وتعالى
rows.claim: A saying in the Zabur tells David to seek the pious, or scholars, or the wise; God will not destroy a people while one of these is among them.
rows.anchor: حادثوا من الناس الأتقاء فإن لم تجدوا فيهم تقيا فحادثوا العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety depends on knowledge, and scholars must be rational though rational people may lack learning; intellect is seed, knowledge its tree, and piety its fruit.
rows.anchor: لأن التقي لا يوجد بدون العلم كما بينا أن الخشية لا تحصل إلا مع العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Gospel passage warns hearers who neglect learning, urges them to seek and practice knowledge, and describes knowledge as an advocate for its possessor before God.
rows.anchor: ويل لمن سمع بالعلم فلم يطلبه كيف يحشر مع الجهال إلى النار

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In a Gospel resurrection dialogue, God assures scholars that their hope for mercy is fulfilled and admits them to Paradise among His righteous servants.
rows.anchor: فيقول : فأني قد فعلت ، إني قد استودعتكم حكمتي لا لشر أردته بكم

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqatil says the Gospel records God telling Jesus to honor scholars, whom God preferred above all creation except prophets and messengers.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان وجدت في الإنجيل . أن الله تعالى قال لعيسى بن مريم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar transmits God's assurance that He placed knowledge in scholars without intending to punish them and will admit them to Paradise despite their deeds.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال قال عليه الصلاة والسلام يقول الله تعالى للعلماء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس
rows.claim: In the Prophet's final Medina sermon, learning humbly and teaching God's servants for God's sake earns the highest reward and rank in Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة وابن عباس : خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطبة بليغة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that those who convey knowledge to Muhammad's community seeking God's face will sit on jeweled golden pulpits without fear until entering Paradise.
rows.anchor: ابن عمر مرفوعا إذا كان يوم القيامة صفت منابر من ذهب

rows.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
rows.claim: Jesus describes Muhammad's community as learned sages, almost prophets in understanding, content with little provision and work, and admitted to Paradise through the testimony of faith.
rows.anchor: عن عيسى ابن مريم عليهما السلام : أن أمة محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام علماء حكماء

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet promises protection from Hell for dust-covered feet seeking knowledge, angelic prayers, and martyr status for one who dies while seeking it.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام ( من اغبرت قدماه في طلب العلم ، حرم الله جسد على النار

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The knowledge-seeker's grave is expanded and illuminated, while a scholar's sleep, study, breath, and tears are credited with worship, charity, and spiritual merit.
rows.anchor: وأربعين قبرا عن يساره ، وأربعين عن خلفه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that insulting a scholar amounts successively to insulting knowledge, the Prophet, Gabriel, and God, who will humiliate the offender.
rows.anchor: فمن أهان العالم فقد أهان العلم ، ومن أهان العلم فقد أهان النبي

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The most generous after Adam is a learned person who spreads knowledge for God and a fighter who dies in God's path; the scholar is raised alone as a community.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( ألا أخبركم بأجود الأجواد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet promises a path to Paradise for seeking knowledge and says Quran study in a mosque brings tranquility, mercy, angelic presence, and God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا ( من نفس عن مؤمن كربة من كرب الدنيا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says prophets, scholars, and martyrs intercede on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( يشفع يوم القيامة ثلاثة : الأنبياء ثم العلماء ثم الشهداء )

rows.speaker: الراوي
rows.claim: The narrator places scholars at the highest rank between prophethood and martyrdom.
rows.anchor: قال الراوي : فأعظم مرتبة هي واسطة بين النبوة والشهادة

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh's report portrays learning as fear of God, worship, struggle, charity, guidance, and life for hearts; angels and creatures pray for scholars, whom God raises as leaders.
rows.anchor: معاذ بن جبل قال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( تعلموا العلم فإن تعلمه لله خشية

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: After death, a person's work continues through ongoing charity, useful knowledge, or a righteous child praying for them.
rows.anchor: إذا مات ابن آدم انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث صدقة جارية ؛ أو علم ينتفع به

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When asked whom to approach for needs, the Prophet names Quran people, then scholars, then bright-faced people.
rows.anchor: إذا سألتم الحوائج فاسألوها الناس قيل يا رسول الله ومن الناس

rows.speaker: الراوي
rows.claim: The narrator explains that 'people of the Quran' means those who memorize its meanings.
rows.anchor: قال الراوي والمراد بأهل القرآن من يحفظ معانيه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet calls one who enjoins right and forbids wrong God's, His Book's, and His Messenger's deputy, and likens worldly life to poison taken in medicinal doses.
rows.anchor: من أمر بالمعروف ونهى عن المنكر فهو خليفة الله في أرضه وخليفة كتابه

rows.speaker: الراوي
rows.claim: The narrator includes scholars among those deputies because they explain what is forbidden and lawful.
rows.anchor: قال الراوي والعلماء داخلون فيه لأنهم يقولون هذا حرام فاجتنبوه وهذا حلال فخذوه

rows.speaker: الخبر
rows.claim: An unnamed report calls the scholar a prophet who has received no revelation.
rows.anchor: في الخبر : العالم نبي لم يوح إليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says one should be a scholar, learner, listener, or lover of learning, never a fifth kind who perishes.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( كن عالما ، أو متعلما ، أو مستمعا ، أو محبا

rows.speaker: الراوي
rows.claim: The narrator reconciles the two-people report by treating listeners and lovers as learners, so only the learned and those learning escape the category of worthless rabble.
rows.anchor: إن المستمع والمحب بمنزلة المتعلم

rows.speaker: أعراب
rows.claim: An Arab advises his son to be a stealthy lion, a lurking wolf, or a vigilant dog, never an incomplete human being.
rows.anchor: كن سبعا خالسا أو ذئبا خانسا أو كلبا حارسا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet promises emancipation for every step when someone leans on a scholar's hand and a good deed for every hair when kissing a scholar's head.
rows.anchor: من اتكأ على يده عالم كتب الله له بكل خطوة عتق رقبة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The heavens and earth grieve when an honored person is humiliated, a rich person impoverished, or a scholar made a plaything by the ignorant.
rows.anchor: برواية أبي هريرة ( بكت السموات / السبع ومن فيهن

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Quran bearers lead the people of Paradise, martyrs command them, and prophets are their masters.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( حملة القرآن عرفاء أهل الجنة والشهداء قواد أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet calls scholars keys to Paradise and deputies of the prophets.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( العلماء مفاتيح الجنة وخلفاء الأنبياء

rows.speaker: الراوي
rows.claim: The narrator says scholars are metaphorical keys because their knowledge opens Paradise; dreaming of holding Paradise's keys signifies religious knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال الراوي الإنسان لا يكون مفتاحا إنما المعنى أن عندهم من العلم مفتاح الجنان

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report assigns 999 of every 1,000 daily mercies to scholars, knowledge-seekers, and Muslims, leaving one for everyone else.
rows.anchor: إن لله تعالى في كل يوم وليلة ألف رحمة على جميع خلقه الغافلين

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In a dialogue with Gabriel, the Prophet ranks knowledge first, then looking at and visiting a scholar; knowledge sought for God and communal good guarantees Paradise.
rows.anchor: قلت يا جبريل أي الأعمال أفضل لأمتي ؟ قال : العلم ، قلت ثم أي ؟

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet names scholars and learners among ten people whose prayers are answered, alongside the virtuous, vulnerable, pilgrims, fighters, and others.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( عشرة تستجاب لهم الدعوة العالم والمتعلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet defines knowledge as a guide for action, intellect as a leader to good, desire as sin's mount, wealth as the arrogant's cloak, and the world as the afterlife's market.
rows.anchor: سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما العلم ؟ فقال : دليل العمل قيل : فما العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man told that he had one hour left asks the Prophet for the best use of it, studies, and dies before sunset; al-Razi infers that learning must be the best deed.
rows.anchor: قال اشتغل بالتعلم فاشتغل بالتعلم ، وقبض قبل المغرب

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A famous report says all people are dead except the learned.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( الناس كلهم موتى إلا العالمون

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports seven continuing benefits after death, beginning with imparting knowledge; al-Razi says teaching leads because spiritual benefit outlasts bodily benefits.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال عليه الصلاة والسلام ( سبعة للعبد تجري بعد موته : من علم علما

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says to sit with scholars when they move people from doubt to certainty, pride to humility, enmity to counsel, ostentation to sincerity, and desire to renunciation.
rows.anchor: لا تجالسوا العلماء إلا إذا دعوكم من خمس إلى خمس

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In counsel to Ali, the Prophet calls monotheism his capital, work his craft, prayer the delight of his eyes, remembrance his heart's vision, and knowledge his inheritance.
rows.anchor: يا علي احفظ التوحيد فأنه رأس مالي والزم العمل فإنه حرفتي

rows.speaker: أبو كبشة الأنصاري
rows.claim: In a four-person parable, the knowledgeable person who uses wealth rightly and the one who wishes to do likewise share reward; the ignorant rich and poor who wish to misuse wealth share blame.
rows.anchor: أبو كبشة الأنصاري قال ضرب لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل الدنيا مثل أربعة رهط

rows.speaker: كميل بن زياد
rows.claim: Ali divides people into a Godly scholar, a learner on the path to salvation, and ignorant rabble; knowledge protects and grows when shared, while wealth dwindles, and knowledge remains a person's adornment and judge.
rows.anchor: كميل بن زياد قال أخذ علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه بيدي فأخرجني إلى الجبانة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar says a sinner may leave a scholar's gathering repentant and sinless, and that no soil is more honored than scholars' gatherings.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : إن الرجل ليخرج من منزله وعليه من الذنوب مثل جبل تهامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Solomon chose knowledge over kingship and wealth, yet received knowledge and the kingdom together.
rows.anchor: عنم ابن عباس خير سليمان بين الملك والمال وبين العلم فاختار العلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked why Solomon used the hoopoe to find water, Ibn Abbas says it could see beneath the earth like glass; when challenged about covered traps, he answers that fate blinds sight.
rows.anchor: عن نافع بن الأرزق قال لابن عباس كيف اختار سليمان الهدهد لطلب الماء

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id says 9,999 of Paradise's 10,000 portions belong to those who understood God's command through their intellect, and one to righteous poor believers.
rows.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخدري تقسم الجنة على عشرة آلاف جزء تسعة آلاف وتسعمائة وتسعة وتسعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas advises his son to pursue good manners, which aid dignity and companionship, provide comfort and standing, and elevate the lowly.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس لولده يا بني عليك بالأدب فإنه دليل على المروءة

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri says scholars' pen-scratching is glorification, writing and reading are worship, their ink resembles martyrs' blood, and they will be honored with the prophets.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن البصري : صرير قلم العلماء تسبيح وكتابة العلم والنظر فيه عبادة

rows.speaker: كتاب كليلة ودمنة
rows.claim: Kalila wa-Dimna says scholars, rulers, and brothers must not be slighted: disrespecting each damages religion, worldly life, or personal honor respectively.
rows.anchor: في ( كتاب كليلة ) ودمنة : أحق من لا يستخف بحقوقهم ثلاثة : العالم والسلطان والإخوان

rows.speaker: سقراط
rows.claim: Socrates says knowledge is superior because no one can serve it to you as they can other things, and nobody can take it from you.
rows.anchor: قال سقراط من فضيلة العلم أنك لا تقدر على أن يخدمك فيه أحد

rows.speaker: بعض الحكماء
rows.claim: A wise man's retort says one may close the eyes, ears, or mouth, but cannot stop oneself from learning.
rows.anchor: قيل لبعض الحكماء لا تنظر فأغمض عينيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A humorous legal anecdote says a learned thief, drinker, or adulterer could evade punishment by offering a legal-sounding excuse for the act.
rows.anchor: إذا كان السارق عالما لا تقطع يده لأنه يقول كان المال وديعة لي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One speaker urges reviving brothers' hearts with explanatory insight as vegetation revives dead land, since a soul distanced from desires and doubts is better than fertile soil.
rows.anchor: أحيوا قلوب إخوانكم ببصائر بيانكم كما تحيون الموات بالنبات والنواة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet equates ignorance with death before burial and says one not revived by knowledge has no resurrection; al-Razi uses the poem to praise learning.
rows.anchor: وإن امرأ لم يحيى بالعلم ميت … وليس له حتى النشور نشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sin committed in ignorance seems unlikely to cease, while knowledge makes repentance possible: Adam sought forgiveness, whereas Satan persisted in error through ignorance.
rows.anchor: انظر إلى زلة آدم فإنه بعلمه استغفر والشيطان غوى وبقي في غيه أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's minister defended him with a Quranic argument and thereby deserved a share in his kingdom; by analogy, defending true religion with proof merits God's favor.
rows.anchor: إن كان قميصه قد من * دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A would-be royal servant is told to learn; once knowledge opens his eyes, he chooses service to God, realizing the true master is the Lord.
rows.anchor: كنت أهلا لخدمتك حين لم ترني أهلا لخدمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of worldly life obstructs learning: a tiny object over the eye's dark surface blocks physical sight, so the whole world covering the heart's pupil blocks inward sight.
rows.anchor: إذا وضعت على سواد عينك جزءا من الدنيا لا ترى شيئا

rows.speaker: حكيم
rows.claim: A sage traces knowledge from heart and seeking through study and debate, but debate alone is barren; knowledge joined to action bears an everlasting kingdom.
rows.anchor: وإذا ظهر بالمناظرة فهو عقيم ونتاجه بالعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi reads the ant's warning in 27:18 as exonerating Solomon: prophets are protected from sin, and any crushing would be inadvertent; the ant's knowledge wins leadership, so fuller knowledge merits leadership.
rows.anchor: فقوله تعالى : { وهم لا يشعرون } إشارة إلى تنزيه الأنبياء عليهم السلام عن المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As training makes a dog's impure catch pure, knowledge of God may purify souls naturally pure but stained by sin, turning the rejected into the accepted through divine mercy.
rows.anchor: فههنا النفس والروح طاهرتان في أصل الفطرة إلا أنهما تلوثتا بأقذار المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart rules the limbs because of knowledge, not strength, size, or sharpness; therefore knowledge is the noblest attribute.
rows.anchor: وإنما تلك الرياسة بسبب العلم فدل على أن العلم أشرف الصفات

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf rejects amputation in a theft case: admitting to taking property proves liability but not theft, and a later theft admission cannot cancel that established liability.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو يوسف : لا قطع عليه

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Under threat from al-Hajjaj, Yahya ibn Ya'mar proves Hasan and Husayn descend from the Prophet: Jesus is counted among Noah's descendants despite having no human father, so maternal descent counts; al-Hajjaj releases him.
rows.anchor: وهو قوله : { ونوحا هدينا من قبل ومن ذريته * داوود * وسليمان }

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that when a group accepts its chosen representative as imam, that imam's Quran recitation counts as theirs; his Medina interlocutors accept the logic.
rows.anchor: قالوا : لأنا رضينا به إماما فكان قوله قولا لنا
